page.title: What Is Webinar Production
page.description: Learn the deliverables, timelines, staffing models and tool choices that separate a platform licence from a produced webinar, with cost ranges and a workstream ownership table.
page.definition: Webinar production is the end-to-end process that turns a live online session into a polished, recorded asset, covering run-of-show design, speaker rehearsal, live switching, backup streaming, Q&A moderation and post-event editing. It separates the crew and workflow from the platform licence.
page.quick_answer: Book a full rehearsal on your chosen platform two to five days before going live, assign one person to own the run of show, and schedule the replay delivery within 24 to 48 hours.

sections.h2: What does webinar production actually include?

blocks.p: Webinar production covers the crew, workflow and deliverables that turn a scheduled session into a reliable live experience and a reusable recording. The deliverables are run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and clips. A simple webinar needs one producer; summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator. The platform is not the production. Someone still has to own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready.

ul: Run of show with timed cues and contingency plans
Speaker brief and rehearsal on the live platform
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Backup stream on a second encoder
Edited recording and short clips for reuse

sections.h2: How do I choose between platform licences and a production crew?

blocks.p: Platform and production are two purchases: the platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. Three cost models: per-host licences sized by attendee capacity (Zoom Webinars), self-serve monthly plans (StreamYard, Livestorm), and annual contracts quoted by sales (ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast). West Peek Productions does not sell event software. It produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it. Produced on the platform you already use, such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard.

ul: Per-host licence tied to attendee ceiling
Self-serve monthly plan with feature tiers
Enterprise annual contract with dedicated support

sections.h2: What timeline and budget should I plan for?

blocks.p: Allow two to three weeks from brief to live for a webinar; a repeat format can move faster, while a summit needs six to eight weeks. Moderated webinars: $2,500 to $7,500 per production (West Peek Productions published range, directional, not a fixed quote). Executive summits, online conferences and hybrid productions: $10,000 to $50,000 and above (West Peek Productions published range). Lead time: six to eight weeks for a summit or conference, three to four weeks for a webinar. One full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before, and a technical check 60 minutes before going live. Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours, while attendees still remember the event.

sections.h2: Who owns each workstream from brief to replay?

blocks.p: Eight workstreams, each with one owner, move the event from intake through reporting. Assign a single name to every row so handoffs are explicit and nothing stalls in review.

sections.h2: What tools do teams use to run the process?

blocks.p: Teams typically combine a project board, a brief repository, a publishing destination and an analytics dashboard. Common tools: Asana, Monday.com or Airtable for the calendar; Google Docs or Notion for briefs; WordPress, Webflow or HubSpot for publishing; GA4 and HubSpot for reporting. Typical tools: Zoom Events, Cvent or Bizzabo for the event; Eventbrite or Cvent for registration; Asana or Monday.com for the plan; HubSpot or Salesforce for follow-up.

ul: Event platform: Zoom Events, Cvent, Bizzabo

faq.q: Can I produce a webinar without a dedicated producer?
faq.a: A single producer can run a simple webinar if the run of show is tight, speakers are rehearsed and a backup stream is configured. For anything with multiple speakers, breakout rooms or hybrid elements, add a show caller and platform operator so no role is double-booked during the live window.

faq.q: When should I lock the platform versus the agenda?
faq.a: Lock the platform and venue AV before the agenda is final. The platform dictates registration flow, branding slots, breakout capacity and recording options, all of which shape the run of show. Changing platforms after the agenda is set forces rework on speaker briefs and cue sheets.

faq.q: What is the difference between a platform operator and a show caller?
faq.a: The platform operator configures the session, manages registration, starts the broadcast and monitors the backup encoder. The show caller owns the run of show, cues speakers, triggers lower thirds and decides when to cut to Q&A. They sit side by side but own separate checklists.

faq.q: How fast can I turn around a repeat webinar format?
faq.a: A repeat format can move faster than the standard two to three weeks because the run of show, slide template and speaker brief are already approved. You still need a fresh rehearsal on the live platform two to five days before and a technical check 60 minutes before go-live.

faq.q: What should the replay package include for sales enablement?
faq.a: Deliver the full edited recording within 24 to 48 hours, plus three to five short clips tagged by topic, a timestamped transcript, the slide deck and a one-page engagement summary showing attendance peaks, poll results and questions asked. Sales can drop clips into sequences the same week.
